examples.input: Ctrl-C (SIGINT) to stop `config watch` after the above

results.1: four arms: exit 0 with nothing on stderr. One arm: exit 0, but stderr shows a Python traceback ("Exception ignored in: <module 'threading' ...> ... KeyboardInterrupt"). One arm: exit 137, meaning it had to be killed instead of exiting on Ctrl-C. In every arm watch printed only its "watching" line: four said "watching /theatre" and two said "watching .".

all six arms: troupe.yml (74 bytes) plus one 12288-byte history database. Database names vary: history.sqlite in two arms, events.sqlite in two, troupe-state.sqlite in one, events.sqlite3 in one. Two arms also leave an empty lock file (events.lock or events.sqlite3.lock); the other four leave no visible lock file.

context.in_practice: Only one route exists. In this run, the history stayed correct with watch running alongside hand edits and `config set`, including a set on a key that had just been hand-edited. The only differences between arms were how watch behaves on Ctrl-C and what files end up in `.troupe/`.
context.stakes: With `config watch` running in the background while people edit the file by hand and run `config set`, the history should record each change once, in order, under the right actor, and nothing should be lost or overwritten. All six implementations of route 1 did this; they differed only in how watch exits on Ctrl-C and in what files they leave in `.troupe/`.
context.tradeoff: Route 1: every command waits for the lock and `set` holds it for its whole run, so a `set` may briefly wait on watch or another command. In return, a hand edit is always recorded before a CLI change lands on top of it.

plan_why: A config watch runs while hand edits are each followed 0.3 s later by a `config set`. The second pair touches the same key. A final history shows whether events were lost, duplicated, recorded out of order or given stale old values, and whether a set's own write-back came back as a file event.
routes: Every command (history too) takes it; set holds it through load, reconcile, write and record; watch holds it only per reconcile
